Title: Development of a Flexible Coupling Framework for Coastal Inundation Studies
Brief Abstract: To enable flexible model coupling in coastal inundation studies, a coupling framework based on ESMF/NUOPC technology under a common modeling framework called the NOAA Environmental Modeling System (NEMS) was developed. The framework is essentially a software wrapper around atmospheric, wave and storm surge models that enables its components communicate seamlessly, and efficiently run in massively parallel environments. We implemented the coupled application including ADCIRC and unstructured WWAVEWATCHIII caps as well as NUOPC compliant caps to read Hurricane Weather Research and Forecasting Model (HWRF) generated forcing fields. We validated the coupled application for a laboratory test and a full scale inundation case of the Hurricane Ike, 2008, on a high resolution mesh covering the whole US Atlantic coast. We showed that how nonlinear interaction between surface waves and total water level results in significant enhancements and progression of the inundation and wave action into land in and around the hurricane landfall region. We also presented that how the maximum wave setup and maximum surge regions may happen at the various time and locations depending on the storm track and geographical properties of the landfall area.

Title: UFS Weather Model (Umbrella Repository)

It integrates various Earth system components-including atmosphere (FV3), ocean (MOM6/HYCOM), sea ice (CICE6), wave (WW3), and land (Noah-MP) models-using the CMEPS mediator. It serves as the foundation for NOAA's next-generation operational numerical weather prediction suite, supporting applications from short-range to seasonal timescales.

Title: NOAA/NCEP Global Workflow (GWF)
Brief Abstract: The Global Workflow is a complex system of interconnected batch jobs that manage the operational cycling of the Global Forecast System (GFS). It coordinates the end-to-end process of numerical weather prediction, including data ingestion, atmospheric analysis (GSI/EnKF), the execution of the UFS Weather Model, post-processing, and verification. It is designed to run in production via ecFlow and for research/development via the Rocoto workflow manager.
Principal Investigators: NOAA Environmental Modeling Center (EMC); lead code managers are David Huber and Rahul Mahajan.

Title: GFDL Finite-Volume Cubed-Sphere Dynamical Core (FV3)
Brief Abstract: This repository contains the source code for the Finite-Volume Cubed-Sphere Dynamical Core (FV3), the atmospheric engine used in the Unified Forecast System (UFS). FV3 is designed to provide high-resolution, global-to-regional atmospheric modeling with excellent computational efficiency and physical consistency. The repository includes the dynamical core, GFDL microphysics, and various drivers and tools necessary for integrating the core into larger Earth system models. It is a critical component for NOAA's Next-Generation Global Prediction System (NGGPS).

Title: GFDL Flexible Modeling System (FMS)
Brief Abstract: The Flexible Modeling System (FMS) is a high-performance software environment that supports the development, execution, and scientific interpretation of atmospheric, oceanic, and climate system models. It provides a standardized infrastructure to handle parallelization, I/O (via fms2_io), data exchange between grids, and time-stepping orchestration. FMS acts as the coupling architecture for many GFDL models, including the FV3 dynamical core, ensuring computational efficiency and portability across diverse high-end computing platforms. Recent updates include enhanced OpenACC support and a rewrite of the Diagnostic Manager to support modern YAML-based configurations.

Title: GFDL Vortex Tracker
Brief Abstract: The GFDL Vortex Tracker is a program used to provide forecast position and intensity estimates for tropical cyclones and other vortices within numerical weather prediction models. It works by tracking the average of the maxima or minima of several parameters (such as relative vorticity, wind circulation, and geopotential height) at multiple atmospheric levels (e.g., 700mb, 850mb, and surface). This multi-parameter approach allows for more accurate tracking of weaker or poorly defined storms. The tracker outputs data in several formats, most notably the Automated Tropical Cyclone Forecasting (ATCF) format required by the National Hurricane Center (NHC). It supports input data in GRIB1, GRIB2, and NetCDF formats and is compatible with both global and regional models.
Principal Investigators: Timothy Marchok (Lead), Caitlyn McAllister, and the GFDL Modeling Systems Division.

Title: Updates Cmake Build System and Other System Set-ups (#59)
Brief Abstract: This pull request introduces significant updates to the GFDL Vortex Tracker's build infrastructure and high-performance computing (HPC) environment support. Key changes include a modernization of the CMake build system to accommodate newer Intel oneAPI compilers (ifx and icx), the addition of a dedicated debug-cmake.sh script for enhanced troubleshooting, and the transition to explicit module versioning across supported UFS machines (including Gaea, Jet, Hera, and WCOSS2). Furthermore, it adds official support for the "Ursa" HPC system. These updates are designed to strengthen model reproducibility, prevent dependency conflicts, and ensure consistent compilation across different Tier 1 research and operational platforms.

Title: GFDL Vortex Tracker - Release 2025.01.01
Brief Abstract: This release of the GFDL Vortex Tracker introduces new diagnostic capabilities for analyzing the vertical tilt of a storm's vortex. Users can now choose between several variables-relative vorticity, wind circulation, geopotential height, or temperature-to determine vortex tilt. The update allows for user-specified vertical levels via a text configuration file, with the resulting diagnostic data written to a dedicated output file. These enhancements provide meteorologists and researchers with more precise tools for understanding the structural evolution and intensity of tropical cyclones and other tracked atmospheric vortices.

Title: Fix allocatable arrays and allow EMC unit numbers (#63)
Brief Abstract: This update addresses a critical bug in the GFDL Vortex Tracker where unallocated arrays were being accessed under certain flag configurations (such as when sstflag or genflag were not set to 'Y'), which previously caused system segmentation faults (segfaults). The fix introduces conditional logic to ensure arrays like sst, q850, and temperature are only accessed when properly allocated. Additionally, the update incorporates code to support the Environmental Modeling Center (EMC) method of specifying Fortran unit numbers via environmental variables (e.g., "FORT51"), enhancing compatibility with operational UFS workflows while maintaining support for standard file naming conventions.
